answer: For a poll on an onyx prism in the ocean, the server uses a frozen graph of mutually signed connections and a trusted seed. It accepts a ballot only if it can route one unit of flow from the seed to its key without exceeding unit edge capacities used by accepted ballots; otherwise it rejects it. More ballots across a cut require more edges across it, potentially costing recruitment effort. Collusion can create such edges, and poorly connected voters may be excluded.
